stories.headline: Trump reimposes Iran naval blockade and 20% Hormuz cargo toll; oil jumps ~9%, Kospi crashes

key_facts.fact: President Trump reinstated the US naval blockade on Iranian shipping on Monday July 13 and declared that all non-Iranian cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz must pay the US a 20% fee.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump reinstated the U.S. naval blockade on Iranian shipping Monday and declared that all non-Iranian cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz must pay the United States a 20% fee, sending oil prices surging and pushing stocks lower.

key_facts.fact: The move erases the last concession to Iran under the June memorandum of understanding signed at Versailles just 26 days earlier, unraveling the preliminary peace deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The return of the naval blockade erases the last remaining concession to Tehran provided under the memorandum of understanding that was signed by the president at the Palace of Versailles amid great fanfare just 26 days ago.

key_facts.fact: Trump formally notified Congress that US military action against Iran 'commenced on July 7,' in a message dated July 10 released Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: Military action 'commenced on July 7,' the president said in a message dated July 10 and addressed to Republican Sen. Chuck Grassley of Iowa, the Senate's president pro tempore.

key_facts.fact: Oil surged nearly 10%: US crude settled up 9.4% at $78.14 a barrel and Brent up 9.6% at $83.30, while the S&P 500 fell 0.8% and the Nasdaq 1.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. crude settled up 9.4%, or $6.73, to $78.14 a barrel while Brent settled at $83.30 per barrel, up 9.6%, or $7.29.

key_facts.fact: South Korea's Kospi dropped 8.9%, including a 15.4% plunge in SK Hynix, its worst single-day fall since the company began trading in 1997.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea's Kospi index dropped 8.9%, including a 15.4% plunge for SK Hynix stock — its worst single-day decline since the company began trading in 1997.

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi mocked the toll, calling Iran the 'guardian' of the strait and vowing to charge a lower, 'fair' rate; the blockade was set to begin at 2000 GMT Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: The maritime blockade was due to begin at 2000 GMT on Tuesday, the US military said, as oil prices shot up around nine percent after both sides traded attacks.

stories.headline: Fed's Waller says rate hike may be needed 'in the near term' if inflation stays hot

key_facts.fact: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on July 13 the central bank may need to raise interest rates 'in the near term' if data show inflation continuing well above the 2% target, calling monetary policy at a 'crossroads.'
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. central bank may need to raise interest rates 'in the near term' if coming data show inflation continuing well above the 2% target, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Monday, in remarks that characterized monetary policy as being at a 'crossroads.'

key_facts.fact: Waller said core PCE inflation has climbed from 3% in December 2025 to 3.4% in May, past the point where increases can be blamed on earlier tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: I am concerned about the elevated pace of core inflation this year, which has steadily moved up—as measured by the 12-month personal consumption expenditures (PCE) rate—from 3 percent in December 2025 to 3.4 percent in May.

key_facts.fact: He said nearly 70% of core-services categories, which make up 75% of core prices, have 3-month and 12-month inflation running over 3%.
key_facts.excerpt: Of the categories in core services, which account for 75% of core prices, nearly 70% have 3-month and 12-month inflation over 3%, he said.

key_facts.fact: Waller pointed to June CPI due Tuesday and PPI on Wednesday as decisive; markets were pricing about a 40% chance of a July rate hike and overwhelming odds by September.
key_facts.excerpt: Financial markets are pricing about a 40% chance of a policy-rate increase at the Fed's July meeting, and overwhelming odds of a rate hike by September.

key_facts.fact: Waller argued the Fed cannot stand by, saying 'Sternly staring at inflation until it melts before our withering gaze is not an option.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'When inflation is well above its target and the labor market is near full employment and stable, any serious policy rule calls for raising the policy rate to bring down inflation,' he said. 'Sternly staring at inflation until it melts before our withering gaze is not an option.'

stories.headline: Yemen's Houthis strike Saudi airport in biggest flare-up since 2022 truce

key_facts.fact: The internationally recognized Yemeni government bombed the runway of Sanaa airport on July 13 to stop an Iranian plane carrying a Houthi delegation from landing.
key_facts.excerpt: The government forces bombed the runway at the airport on Monday to prevent the landing of a plane carrying a delegation of Houthis arriving from Iran.

key_facts.fact: In response, the Houthis launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted the missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: On Monday evening, the Saudi-led coalition for Yemen reported that it had intercepted ballistic missiles launched by the Iran-backed Houthis towards the southern region of the kingdom. The Houthis later said that they had carried out a military operation targeting Abha International Airport with ballistic missiles and drones.

key_facts.fact: The strikes are the first the Houthis have claimed against Saudi Arabia since an informal truce took effect in March 2022, breaking a four-year lull.
key_facts.excerpt: The strikes are the first claimed by the Houthis against Saudi Arabia since an informal truce went into effect in March 2022 following Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: No casualties were reported, but the Yemeni government closed all airports 'until further notice.'
key_facts.excerpt: No casualties were reported... A statement from the government in the south said that all airports in Yemen were 'closed until further notice, with immediate effect.'

key_facts.fact: UN Yemen envoy Hans Grundberg urged all sides to de-escalate to preserve the relative calm the country has experienced since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Hans Grundberg, UN Special Envoy for Yemen... 'We are urging them to de-escalate and refrain from any actions that would risk a new cycle of violence in Yemen,' he said in a statement.

stories.headline: Ukraine and allies launch anti-ballistic missile coalition; Macron pledges Rafale jets in Paris

key_facts.fact: Ukraine and nine other countries announced on July 13 the formation of an Integrated Anti-Ballistic Missile Coalition to build a shared European ballistic-missile defense, joined by about a dozen defense firms.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine and nine other countries announced Monday they were forming a coalition to protect Europe from ballistic missiles... 'Our goal is to build a shared ballistic missile defense capability for Europe,' the 10 nations said in a statement in Paris.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said the joint 'Freyja' system aims to be a cheaper, mass-produced supplement to the US Patriot, developable within the next 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our work on a joint system – Freyja – is not intended to replace existing systems. It is a way to supplement our defence, create a strong shield over the entirety of Europe and do all of this faster and at a lower cost.'

key_facts.fact: Macron announced Ukraine ordered Franco-Italian air defense systems and 16 Rafale fighter jets to operate in 2028-2029, plus licenses to produce SCALP cruise missiles, Aster-30 SAMs and AASM Hammer bombs.
key_facts.excerpt: Macron announced that Paris will provide Ukraine with Rafale fighter jets, with the first aircraft expected to be delivered in 2028-2029. France will also grant licenses for the production of Aster-30 surface-to-air missiles, SCALP cruise missiles, and AASM Hammer guided bombs.

key_facts.fact: Moldova and North Macedonia joined the Coalition of the Willing, bringing it to 40 countries, and the next summit will be held in Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: He announced that Moldova and North Macedonia had joined the Coalition of the Willing, bringing the total number of participants to 40 countries... 'we agreed to hold our next Coalition of the Willing meeting in Ukraine.'

key_facts.fact: UK PM Keir Starmer secured a deal giving UK defense firms access to contracts funded through the EU's £78 billion (€90 billion) Ukraine Support Loan.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Keir Starmer has today announced a landmark agreement that will give UK defence firms access to contracts funded through the EU's £78 billion (€90 billion) Ukraine Support Loan initiative.

stories.headline: EU and UK impose first joint cyber sanctions on Russia over years-long espionage campaign

key_facts.fact: The EU on July 13 imposed sanctions on nine Russian military officers, hackers and private companies over a years-long cyber-espionage campaign against the bloc.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Union has imposed sanctions on Russian military officers, hackers and private companies, denouncing what it called a years-long cyber-espionage campaign against the bloc.

key_facts.fact: The espionage targeted at least nine countries including France, Germany, Poland, Cyprus, the Netherlands, Austria, Slovakia, Romania and Finland.
key_facts.excerpt: It said France, Germany, Poland, Cyprus, the Netherlands, Austria, Slovakia, Romania and Finland, 'among others,' have been targeted.

key_facts.fact: The UK and EU introduced their first joint UK-EU cyber sanctions package, targeting Russian state actors and criminal networks behind malicious cyber activity.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the UK and the EU introduced the first joint UK-EU cyber sanctions package, targeting Russian state actors and criminal networks responsible for malicious cyber activity.

key_facts.fact: France summoned the Russian ambassador, with FM Jean-Noel Barrot citing a 'vast cyber campaign aimed at sabotage and espionage' across about 10 European countries.
key_facts.excerpt: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said he would summon the Russian ambassador to France and impose sanctions against Russian hackers. He told BFMTV-RMC that the issue is about 'a vast cyber campaign aimed at sabotage and espionage, carried out by Russia in about 10 European countries.'

stories.headline: New Alzheimer's drug targeting brain inflammation shows first human biomarker signal at AAIC

key_facts.fact: NeuroTherapia presented Phase 2a data on July 13 at AAIC 2026 in London for NTRX-07, an oral drug that targets the brain's immune cells via the CB2 receptor pathway rather than amyloid plaques.
key_facts.excerpt: NeuroTherapia, Inc.... will be presenting data from its recently completed Phase 2a clinical trial in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference (AAIC) 2026 during the Monday July 13th poster session.

key_facts.fact: The 28-day, multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial enrolled 48 participants with mild cognitive impairment or mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's, randomized 1:1 to 90 mg/day NTRX-07 or placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: The trial was a 28-day, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed primarily to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of NTRX-07 in 48 participants with mild cognitive impairment or mild-to-moderate AD, randomized 1:1 to NTRX-07 (90 mg/day) or placebo.

key_facts.fact: It produced the first human evidence that a selective CB2 agonist can measurably change biomarkers of nerve damage, with neurofilament light chain stabilizing in the treated group and rising on placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, a selective CB2 receptor agonist produced measurable anti-neuroinflammatory biomarker changes in living Alzheimer's patients. The Phase 2a data, presented Monday in a poster session at the Alzheimer's Association conference in London by Cleveland-based NeuroTherapia, Inc.

key_facts.fact: The result positions neuroinflammation-targeting as a credible complement to the amyloid-clearing drugs that have dominated Alzheimer's research for three decades.
key_facts.excerpt: a mechanistic advance that positions neuroinflammation-targeting as a credible complement to the amyloid-clearing drugs that have dominated the field for three decades.

stories.headline: IBM shares tumble ~20% after warning of disappointing preliminary Q2 revenue

key_facts.fact: IBM disclosed preliminary Q2 2026 revenue of $17.2 billion on July 14, up 1% year over year but below internal expectations, citing weakness in its Infrastructure and Software segments.
key_facts.excerpt: IBM (NYSE: IBM) released preliminary second-quarter 2026 financial results on July 14, disclosing revenue of $17.2 billion, up 1 percent year over year, but below internal expectations due to weakness in its Infrastructure and Software

key_facts.fact: The reported revenue came in below the roughly $17.9 billion analysts had expected, and IBM shares fell about 20% pre-market as CEO Arvind Krishna said customers were shifting spending toward chips.
key_facts.excerpt: IBM reports preliminary Q2 revenue of $17.2B, below $17.9B est., as CEO Arvind Krishna says customers are shifting spending to chips; IBM falls 20% pre-market.
